name: EgoLife Dataset
description: A comprehensive 300-hour egocentric, interpersonal, multiview, and multimodal daily life dataset featuring six participants living together for one week, continuously recording their daily activities using AI glasses for multimodal egocentric video capture, along with synchronized third-person-view video references.
creator: The EgoLife Team
rai:dataCollection: Six participants lived together for one week in a custom-designed environment (EgoHouse), wearing Meta Aria glasses to capture multimodal egocentric videos. Each participant recorded approximately 8 hours of egocentric video and signals daily. Additionally, 15 strategically placed GoPro cameras recorded activities from multiple angles, and millimeter-wave radars provided spatial and motion data for synchronized, comprehensive multimodal analysis. A second session was conducted in Milan with similar setup.
rai:dataCollectionType: Direct measurement, Software Collection, Passive Data Collection
rai:dataCollectionRawData: Raw data sources include: (1) Egocentric video, audio, IMU, and gaze data from 6 Meta Aria glasses worn by participants; (2) Third-person video from 15 GoPro cameras in Beijing and 6 in Milan; (3) Millimeter-wave radar data from 2 TI IWR6843 (60GHz) mmWave monostatic radars in Beijing and 3 radars in Milan; (4) WiFi signal data from 3 Asus RT-AX82U devices in Milan only.
rai:dataCollectionTimeframe: Beijing session: 7 days (specific dates not provided). Milan session: 1 day (specific date not provided).
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Data preprocessing included: (1) Multi-view synchronization of video and signal data from multiple sources using timestamps; (2) De-identification process where all participant faces were blurred to anonymize identities, bystanders' faces and vehicle license plates were blurred, and sensitive screen content was masked; (3) Audio processing to mute sensitive information; (4) Multimodal signal extraction where radar and WiFi data were extracted and aligned with video data; (5) For mmWave data, constant false alarm rate (CFAR) detection algorithm was used to detect dynamic target signals; (6) For WiFi data, channel state information (CSI) was extracted from 802.11ax frames with 160 MHz bandwidth and 4x4 MIMO configuration.
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Annotations were created through multiple stages: (1) Transcript annotations: Speech recognition was applied to generate initial timestamped transcripts, followed by diarization to differentiate speakers, then human review for accuracy; (2) Caption annotations: Videos were split into 5-minute clips and slowed to 0.8x speed, annotators provided continuous detailed narrations by talking, which were converted to text via transcription tool and reviewed; Initial narrations (361K brief phrases) were merged into 25K coherent captions using GPT-4o-mini, then expanded into visual-audio captions by pairing with representative frames and transcripts, summarized by GPT-4o and verified by human annotators; (3) EgoLifeQA annotations: Prompts were designed for five question types (EntityLog, EventRecall, HabitInsight, RelationMap, TaskMaster), visual-audio captions were fed into GPT-4o in batches to generate ~100K timestamped questions per participant, which were provided to annotators as SRT files for filtering and refinement, resulting in 500 high-quality QAs per participant after rigorous selection.
rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: CapCut (ByteDance) for video captioning with dubbing functions; SRT file format for annotation review and verification
rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: For QA annotations, AI-generated questions served as a filtering and inspiration tool for annotators rather than final annotations. Only questions requiring information from at least five minutes prior were retained, with preference for those demanding longer dependencies and strong real-world relevance. Annotators also generated distractors for multiple-choice questions and annotated whether audio was required and specified the look-back time (certification length) necessary for retrieving the correct answer.
rai:annotationsPerItem: For captions: Initial narrations averaged 2.65 seconds per narration (361K total), merged into 25K captions, then expanded into visual-audio captions. For QA: 500 questions per participant (3,000 total for 6 participants), with multiple-choice format including distractors.
rai:machineAnnotationTools: Whisper Large v3 for speech recognition and audio transcription; Open-source diarization algorithm for speaker differentiation; GPT-4o-mini for merging related caption phrases; GPT-4o for expanding captions with visual and speech context and generating initial QA candidates
rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The project is ongoing with plans to expand the dataset to cover a broader range of languages, locations, and activities. A second session (EgoLife-Milan) has been collected featuring primarily English language interactions. Future versions will continue to be released.
rai:personalSensitiveInformation: The dataset captures daily life activities including personal interactions, conversations, shopping, cooking, socializing, and entertainment. Language is a key attribute (Chinese for Beijing session, English/Chinese/Italian for Milan session). All participant faces were blurred for anonymization, and sensitive audio segments were muted to protect privacy.
rai:dataSocialImpact: The EgoButler system and EgoLifeQA dataset hold significant potential to enhance human-AI interaction through personalized assistance and context-aware applications. By enabling AI to understand long-term egocentric perspectives, it could support daily activities, personal organization, and contextual reminders, improving quality of life especially for individuals needing consistent support such as the elderly or those with cognitive challenges. In educational and professional settings, egocentric AI could facilitate learning, task tracking, and skill development. However, as this technology integrates more deeply into personal spaces, it is essential to address privacy and ethical considerations to ensure user autonomy and trust.
rai:dataLimitations: The dataset was intentionally started with a narrow setting to build a strong foundation, sacrificing some generalizability (e.g., single language/scenario in Beijing session, limited to 6 participants, one-week duration). The primary language is Chinese for the main dataset, which may limit applicability to other linguistic contexts. EgoGPT shows limitations including incomplete speech understanding (struggles with human laughter and emotions due to reliance on ASR-trained data), identity recognition challenges (tends to overfit to early observations from Day-1 fine-tuning), and EgoRAG lacks multi-step reasoning capability (performs single-pass search without iterative refinement, prone to failure when relevant information is missing).
rai:dataUseCases: The dataset supports multiple use cases: (1) Training EgoGPT, a lightweight personalized vision-audio-language model for egocentric video understanding; (2) Evaluation on EgoLifeQA benchmark tasks including EntityLog (long-term memory of object details), EventRecall (past events recall), HabitInsight (personal habit patterns), RelationMap (interpersonal interactions), and TaskMaster (task assignment based on prior actions); (3) Development of retrieval-augmented generation systems (EgoRAG) for ultra-long-context question answering; (4) Research on long-duration activities, interpersonal dynamics, and contextual interactions; (5) Advancing egocentric AI assistants for life-oriented assistance.
